method.label: Follow divisor counts by prime pattern

annotationRationale: The divisor-count formula determines the transitions, and iteration identifies which inputs settle at 12. Prime exponent bounds provide an exhaustive classification without duplicate inputs.
sourceMethod: Follows the official classification by prime-factorization form and iteration to the fixed values 8 and 12. Adds explicit bounds proving the classification exhaustive and details the successful counts.

review.mathCheck: The formula F(n)=2∏(a_i+1) gives fixed points 8 and 12. The exhaustive exponent patterns yield exactly 12,18,20,28,32,36,44,45,48,50 as inputs reaching 12; notably 36→18→12 and 48→20→12. Every input stabilizes within four applications, so the answer is 10, choice D.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA Q23, page 11: the same twelve factorization patterns, transitions and successful count 7+1+1+1. The candidate adds valid bounds proving the classification exhaustive.
review.annotationCheck: The argument includes n=1 and n=50, proves the successful families disjoint and justifies the fiftieth iterate. Statement, choices and key agree with the source; no figure is required.
